title: The IKEA effect: why you overvalue what you build
_format: 1080x1350 = 4:5. NICHT 3:4 — die Instagram-API akzeptiert beim automatischen Veroeffentlichen nur 4:5 bis 1.91:1. Bildprompts bleiben 3:4, ihre schwarze Fusszone faengt die Differenz ab.
_syntax: [Klammern] = Akzentfarbe mit Textur (nur in headline). **Sterne** = fett in bullets/body. Zeilenumbruch = eigener Array-Eintrag. `alt` pro Slide ist Pflicht — Buffer verlangt altText beim Upload.

caption.kern: Same black storage box, same price tag. People who assembled it themselves bid 63% more than people who were handed it already built. 📦🤯
caption.detail: Norton, Mochon and Ariely gave 52 students a plain IKEA box. Half had to build it from the flat pack, half got it assembled. Then everyone bid on it: builders $0.78, non-builders $0.48. Builders also liked the box more (3.81 vs 2.50 on a 7-point scale). In a second test, 106 people folded an origami crane or frog: builders valued their own paper at $0.23, strangers offered $0.05. Builders priced their amateur folds almost like the work of experts ($0.27).
caption.kontext: It only works if you finish. A third group got the same box but stopped two steps early, with every piece in hand and little effort left: they bid $0.59. Those who finished it bid $1.46, more than twice as much. In a Lego version, people who built a set and then took it apart lost the bonus. The authors' read: a finished creation is evidence of your own competence, and people pay extra for that proof, DIY fans and non-DIY people alike.
caption.frage: What is the one thing you built yourself that you would never sell, even though it is objectively worse than the shop version?
caption.sources: Sources: Norton, Mochon & Ariely — The IKEA Effect: When Labor Leads to Love • Journal of Consumer Psychology 22(3): 453–460, 2012

headline: EVEN [AMATEUR ORIGAMI]
FELT LIKE [A TREASURE]
slides.body: 106 people folded a [crane] or a [frog]. Builders priced their own at [$0.23]; strangers offered [$0.05], nearly [five times] less. Yet builders valued their folds almost like the [expert-made] ones: [$0.27].

headline: IT ONLY WORKS IF YOU [FINISH]
BECAUSE IT PROVES YOU [CAN]
slides.body: A third group stopped [two steps] early, every piece in hand: they bid [$0.59]. Finishers bid [$1.46], more than [double]. The authors' read: a finished creation is [proof of your competence], and that is what people pay extra for.
